newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu seeks formula for Syria peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu seeks formula for Syria peace talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told parliament on Monday a "bridging formula" was being sought between Israeli and Syrian positions to restart stalled peace talks between the countries.

"We are seeking now a bridging formula between those two opposite positions," he said, explaining Israel views the Golan Heights it captured from Syria in 1967 as a "vital strategic asset," while Syria wants the plateau back.
"I suppose with good will on both sides and the help of the United States we can reach a formula to renew direct talks with Syria," he said.

Netanyahu addressed parliament on the Syrian issue after 40 opposition members demanded in writing he appear at the debate. Israel broke off halting talks with Syria last March after a series of suicide bombings by Palestinians in Israel.
Netanyahu unseated former Prime Minister Shimon Peres in elections last May.
On Monday Netanyahu appointed Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai to head security negotiations with Syria "if and when such negotiations open," a statement from his office said.
